name: Chess Board
summary: A Synthetic Field (Field Notes no. 5). Battle message: “Opening variation set.”

effects.text: All Pokémon in the teams of both the player and the opponent are assigned roles as chess pieces, based on certain criteria. Each Pokémon can only have one role. If there are two teams on one side, roles are assigned separately for the two teams.
Pawn (The Pokémon is sent out on the first turn of the battle. This role overrides Rook, Bishop, Knight and King.): The Pokémon gains the effect of Sturdy.
Rook (The Pokémon's highest stat is its Defense or Special Defense): Defense and Special Defense are raised by one stage on switch-in.
Bishop (The Pokémon's highest stat is its Attack or Special Attack): Attack and Special Attack are raised by one stage on switch-in.
Knight (The Pokémon's highest stat is its Speed): The Pokémon deals 3x damage when the target is a Queen, and 1.25x damage when using a move in a double battle that targets both opponents.

Queen (The Pokémon is in the final slot of the team (overrides all other roles; limited to one per team)): Defense and Special Defense are raised by one stage on switch-in, and the Pokémon deals 1.5x damage.

King (The Pokémon holds a King's Rock, or has the lowest maximum HP among team members. This role overrides Rook, Bishop and Knight and is limited to one per team.): The priority of any move used by the Pokémon is increased by 1.
Therefore, the roles take precedence in the following order: Queen > Pawn > King > Rook/Bishop/Knight.
There is a machine in the room to the left of the first chess puzzle area in Vanhanen Castle that informs the player of the roles of all Pokémon in the player's current party for a double battle.
Queenly Majesty additionally causes the bearer to deal 1.5x damage. This boost does not stack with the Queen piece boost.

Flying-type Pokémon do not become grounded even though susceptible to Ground moves.
